Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis MedTech Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Moreno, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis MedTech demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance. We'll start with the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives, then move to capital equipment versus consumables mix trends, competitive dynamics and market share trends, key assumptions underlying our guidance, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, FDA approvals and CE marks obtained, and finally organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials, Raj will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Lisa will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Let's begin with the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives. These efforts have been foundational to our strong financial performance, delivering 8% core revenue growth, 220 basis points of gross margin expansion to 68.5%, and adjusted EPS of $1.42, up 12% year-over-year. On pricing, we've maintained disciplined ASP management in a tough reimbursement environment. In our Cardiovascular segment, which is 35% of total revenue and features structural heart devices like our next-gen TAVR valves similar to leading platforms, we saw a 3.2% ASP uplift sequentially, thanks to a favorable mix shift where premium robotic-assisted procedures grew 15% year-over-year, driving higher-margin consumables at $2,500 per case compared to $1,800 for legacy systems. In Neuromodulation, our deep brain stimulation leads for Parkinson's achieved a 4.1% ASP increase to $28,000 per implant kit, backed by real-world data showing 22% better long-term battery life versus competitors like Boston Scientific's Vercise.

Regionally, U.S. pricing gained 2.8% despite CMS's 2024 OPPS final rule reducing TAVR reimbursements by 1.9%; we countered with value-based contracts covering 45% of hospital volume, bundling remote monitoring for $4,200 in annual recurring revenue per patient. In Europe, despite HTA pressures from NICE and IQWiG on elective ortho implants, we raised ASPs 2.5% on hip resurfacing systems to €12,500, supported by superior clinical outcomes that secured 18% market share in Germany. Emerging markets like China and India focused on volume at flat pricing, with peripheral stents at $1,200 ASP, aided by our JV with Sinomed for NMPA fast-tracking.

Technically, our AI-driven dynamic pricing via Salesforce Health Cloud has optimized list-to-net, cutting rebates 150 basis points to 22% of gross sales, while surgeon loyalty programs with co-branded training secured 75% repeat business in endoscopy. On cost management, we generated $185 million in run-rate savings, driving 60% of gross margin gains as COGS fell 180 basis points to 31.5%. We hedged 70% of nitinol needs at $45 per kg, 15% below spot amid volatility. Manufacturing lean sigma programs in Galway, Ireland, and Tijuana, Mexico, cut insulin pump cycle times 28%, saving $62 million, and cobots reduced labor 22% per unit with yields up to 99.2%.

R&D spend focused 65% of our $1.2 billion budget on high-ROI areas like bioresorbable scaffolds and AI imaging for vascular access, trimming non-core by 8%. SG&A leveraged Veeva CRM for $45 million savings in travel and admin. In Asia-Pacific, nearshoring 40% sourcing to Vietnam slashed freight 35%, and U.S. ortho qualified 90% under USMCA to avoid $28 million tariffs. These are embedded in our MedTech 2027 framework, targeting 2-3% annual ASP growth via premiums like our FDA-cleared pulsed-field ablation catheters, priced 18% above thermal competitors. Savings reinvest in digital surgery with Siemens Healthineers, eyeing 300 basis points margin expansion by FY2026. Risks like IRA spillover or Eurozone inflation are buffered by 45% EBITDA margins. Overall, these drove $210 million incremental profit—40% of operating income growth—outpacing peers' flat ASPs.

Now, shifting to capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. This razor-razorblade model underpins our 72% gross margins, with Q3 shifting to 68% consumables and 32% capital, the strongest ever, up from 65%/35% last year. Capital includes high-ASP platforms like our PrecisionNav neuro-navigation akin to StealthStation and EndoFlex suites at $1.2 million ASP. Consumables are annuity drivers: single-use catheters, guidewires, scopes, and kits attaching to our 12,500-system base.

Consumables hit $428 million, up 14% reported or 16% organic, with 12% global procedure growth and 9% neurovascular utilization to 85%, matching da Vinci levels. NovaFlex steerable kits took 22% U.S. TAVR share versus Sapien, ASPs +3%. Capital was $203 million, down 4% YoY but flat sequentially, ASPs +6% to $1.15 million on PrecisionNav 3.0 AI imaging. We placed 175 endoscopy systems, but ortho capex softened 15% on reimbursement.

TTM recurring is 67%, beating Stryker's 62%, adding 220 basis points to margins—82% on consumables vs. 55% capital. U.S. at 71% mix up 400 basis points on ASC growth; EMEA 65% with HTA wins; APAC ex-China 72%; China 60% stabilizing via Mindray JVs. R&D at $180 million YTD boosted PrecisionNav firmware utilization 7%, and Vitalis Sentinel TAVR eyes $100 million consumables by '26. Full-year consumables guide 15-17% organic, mix to 69%; capital rebounds 5-8% on $500 million backlog. This flywheel positions us in the $550 billion market at 5.5% CAGR.

Moving on to competitive dynamics and market share trends. The $550 billion medtech market grows at 6.2% CAGR to 2028 amid demographics and value-based care, but faces GPO pricing, CMS NTAP, and supply issues. We hit 8.7% global share in cardio, ortho, neuromodulation—up 110 basis points—strongest since Q4 2022 on 14% U.S. volumes and Harmony robotics. Units: 12.3% structural heart, overtaking Edwards in TAVR with Evolut-compatible valves at 22% premium.

Ortho at 15.2% share, clawing 1.8 points via Apex Navigation AI planning; Trinity stems +28% volumes vs. Stryker Triathlon, 15% fewer revisions. Monitoring Zimmer Persona IQ, but our Bluetooth trackers hold 92% loyalty. Cardio: Sentinel Ultra at 31% LAA vs. Watchman 42%; EluNIR stents 9.4% share, 4.2% lower MACE. APAC China +2.5 to 11.2%. U.S. 18.1% on PulseSelect PFA disrupting cryo; Europe 7.9% rebounding with ReviNeuro DBS; EM 6.3%. $450 million R&D on AI OrthoAI (96% accuracy), ESG cuts 28%, M&A like $1.2 billion NeuroStim to #2 SCS. Expect intensity from da Vinci 6, but Harmony gains 15-20% robotics share.

Next, key assumptions underlying our guidance, reaffirmed at $4.85-$5.05 billion revenue (8-12% reported, 6-9% organic), EPS $6.75-$7.05, op margins 28.5-29.5%. Procedural volumes 4-6% global; structural heart 10-12% on 15% U.S. TAVR, 8% Europe. Coronary flat-2% U.S., 12-15% EMAX. Pricing flat to -1-2% U.S., offset by structural heart mix to 45%, $32k TAVR ASP; China +5%. Gross 68-69% on Galway scale. Share gains 100-150 bps from $450 million R&D: VascuClip Ultra Q4, AI FFR, Renova RF. U.S. 7-10%, Europe 5%, APAC/EMAX 15%; FX USD/EUR 1.08. Inflation 2.5-3%, capex $250 million, tax 16.5%, no recession. Visibility from 25k accounts, $2.1 billion backlog.

Then, revenue and margin guidance. Q3: $1.22-$1.27 billion (9-14% reported, 8-13% organic). Interventional cardio $680-700 million (12-16%), FlexSense EP +15%; robotics $310-325 million (10-14%), PrecisionArm consumables +20%; ortho $185-195 million flat-5%; emerging $45-55 million 25-40%. U.S. 10-15%, EMEA 8-12%, APAC 5-10%. Gross 68.5-69.5%, op ex 45-46%, EPS $1.45-1.55. FY24 raised to $4.85-$4.95 billion (9-12% reported, 8-11% organic), gross 68-69%, op 22-23%, EPS $5.90-$6.10. Drivers: 9-10% organic (6% volume, 2% pricing, 1% share), 1-2% M&A, synergies.

Now, FDA approvals and CE marks. Transformative quarter: 510(k) for AeroFlow Sirolimus DCB for PAD, 8 months post-submission via Breakthrough, superior 0.22mm lumen loss, 93% patency; Q4 launch targeting $2.8B market at 20-25% premium. PMA for VascuPulse PFA, 78.4% AFib freedom vs. 73.3%, <90-min procedures; $85M peak U.S. by 2027. CE marks under MDR for AeroFlow, VascuPulse, TriFlow TAVR (98.2% stability), 14 months via MATRIX registry; Q1 2025 EU launch, 15% <23mm share. Asia subs PMDA/NMPA; boosts FY25 devices $320M, NPV $2.8B.

Finally, organic revenue growth by segment and geography. FY23 9.4% organic (Q4 11.2%), accelerating from 7.2%. Volumes +8.1%, ASP +1.2%. Cardio 38% revenue, 13.5% (Q4 16.2%) on VitalFlow Ultra 22% U.S. TAVR share, RhythmSync +20%. Ortho 25%, 7.8% (9.1%) on Trinity ASCs, OrthoBot 1,200 bases. MIS 22%, 15.7% (18.4%) PrecisionArm 450 installs, 85% util. Diabetes/Neuro 15%, 5.2% GlucoLink +11%. U.S. 65% 10.1% (12.3%); EMEA 20% 6.8% (8.2%); APAC 10% 14.2% (17.5%) China JV; ROW 5% 9.5%. 28% revenue new products; FY24 8-10%.

I will now turn the call over to Michael for a review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter, with Q2 revenue of $1.24 billion, up 10% organically, gross margins at 68.5%, and adjusted operating income up 15%. Expenses were controlled, with R&D at 12% of revenue and SG&A leveraging efficiencies for 100 basis points improvement. Cash flow from operations hit $350 million, supporting $200 million in share repurchases. Full-year outlook remains robust as detailed.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of PrecisionNav 3.0 and VascuPulse PFA is progressing well, and we anticipate they will revolutionize neuro-navigation and AFib treatment with superior safety and efficiency profiles. R&D pipeline includes five launches this year, backed by $450 million investment, focusing on AI/ML integration, bioresorbables, and robotics enhancements. We're on track for H1 2025 approvals, de-risking $1.2 billion in future revenue from structural heart and EP expansions.

Next, Lisa with insights on our commercial strategy.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Raj. Our commercial team has been instrumental in driving adoption, expanding to 45% ASC penetration and securing value-based contracts across 40% of U.S. volume. We're enhancing customer engagement through surgeon training, digital platforms like VascuTrack, and targeted EM JVs, growing APAC 15%. Directed sales ensure 60% consumables attach rates, positioning us for share gains in robotics and TAVR.

Now, back to Elena for Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, can you elaborate on the key assumptions for FY24 guidance, especially procedural volumes in structural heart amid any macro softness?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, our mid-single-digit procedural assumption holds firm at 4-6% globally, with structural heart at 10-12% driven by 15% U.S. TAVR growth per CRT data and label expansions like VascuClip Ultra. EMAX adds 12-15%, offsetting any U.S. payer scrutiny. Visibility from our hospital contracts gives us confidence.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. Michael, on competitive dynamics, how are you gaining share in cardio against Boston Sci and Edwards, and any pricing impacts?

Michael Chen:
Emily, thanks. We're up 110 basis points to 8.7% share via Sentinel Ultra's 31% LAA penetration and EluNIR's lower MACE, plus PulseSelect PFA disrupting cryo. Pricing disciplined at +1.5% net, with premiums in TAVR offsetting GPO pressure. Ortho Apex clawed back from Stryker with registry data.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Hi team, on commercial side, Lisa, how do consumables mix trends factor into your ASC strategy, and outlook?

Lisa Moreno:
David, consumables at 68% mix, highest ever, with 71% in U.S. on 18% ASC procedure growth. PrecisionArm and NovaFlex attach at 60-75%, driving 16% organic recurring growth. FY guide 69% mix supports margin expansion amid site-neutral shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
Thanks. Raj, with recent FDA wins like VascuPulse, what's the pipeline timeline and R&D ROI?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Rachel, VascuPulse PMA positions us in $4.5B ablation at 12% CAGR, with 78.4% efficacy and Q4 ramp. AeroFlow DCB and TriFlow follow, PMDA/NMPA mid-2025. $450M R&D yields 2.8x NPV, 40% reinvested in AI like PulseAI for 22% faster procedures.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
